paragraphs: CONVERTING JAGGAER .csv INTO EXCEL The easiest method, which seems to work for most people:
1. Open in Excel, separating in columns
2. Edit in Excel, save as csv, close
3. Open the file in Notepad
4. “Replace all” double quotes with commas OR “replace all” semicolons with commas
5. Re-save
Thoughts from Matt Boge, Product Manager
CSV files in Excel

In my experience, some of the issues when dealing with .CSV have to do with the way Excel automatically formats the data when opening a CSV file. For example, when a text field contains only numbers, Excel will interpret this and auto-format the data as a “number”. Where this becomes a problem is when the value isn’t supposed to be a number (eg. a “part number”) and has zeros at the beginning. In this case, when Excel auto-formats to a number, if will interpret these zeros as leading zeros and strip them from the results – which makes the result not match the original.

What I’ve had to do in situations where the CSV has data that Excel isn’t interpreting correctly, is to force Excel to use the text import wizard. When using the import wizard, the user can explicitly define the format of the columns being imported.

One way to do this is to rename the file and give it a file extension of .txt (this won’t affect the underlying data at all). When opening the file with Excel (you may have to change the filter in the Open dialog box to include TXT files), Excel will automatically start the Import Wizard – where you can manually format all columns as “Text” (I automatically choose all columns as text, because Excel will not just reformat numbers, but dates and times, too). There are other options you can choose during this import wizard to help Excel understand the data – like identifying the delimiter; how to treat consecutive delimiters; what the “text qualifiers” are, etc…
An alternative method to renaming the file, is to create a new blank sheet and import “From Text”… which will force Excel to go through the Text Import Wizard (see screenshots)
When saving the file as a CSV, make sure all columns are marked as “Text” to avoid Excel automatically formatting (and changing!) the
Exporting/Saving Excel to CSV

When exporting from Excel… if you choose CSV, then I think it can be confusing. Excel does some odd things. First, they will only put the double-quotes (“) around the text if a specific cell contains a comma… but if you are in some countries where they switch the commas and periods, then I think it will use semi-colons to separate the cells?
As a rule, Excel will look to your system to determine which country you are in and the formatting to use. You can override this there, if that would be easier…
Thoughts from Alastair McMullan (Nov. 2018)

Generally speaking comma delimited files are not a good practice for integrations or user interface uploads, as commas may appear in text, numbers, etc. in both English and non-English speaking countries.
This is solved by two approaches:
1. Pipe delimited files for integrations (instead of using comma-delimited files), or pipe qualified delimited files (even more robust)

2. Excel for User Interface managed uploads (since Excel will change the comma for the point and vice-versa based on the user’s own settings). In JA all of the file upload features are managed through Excel, never through CSV files.
From Aniela Radu, UK Office
Below the steps I’ve performed to solve the formatting issues when extracting/opening .csv JAGGAER files into excel:
This is an excel setting
On your PC, go to “control panel” -> click on “Clock, Language and Region”
Then click on “Change the date, time, or number format”
“Format” – select “English (UK) from the list and then click on “Additional Settings”
For “List separator” should be “,”
And it works brilliantly for me.
NOTE: Some JI training participants have used an online converter effectively. It’s found at jsonformatter.org.
